name: Black supremacy
summary: Black supremacy is a label for doctrines holding that black people are inherently superior to other races, best documented in the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (to 1975), which taught that whites were a bred race of devils whose 6,000-year rule had ended. Its program was rejection of integration, a separate black state funded by the former slave-owning nation, black economic self-reliance, strict moral and gender discipline, and refusal of military service.
scope: Represents the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (c. 1934-1975) as the best-documented black supremacist doctrine, with Malcolm X's 1963 statement of its program. Excludes the post-1975 mainstream Islam of W. Deen Mohammed, Black Hebrew Israelite groups, Nuwaubians, Rastafari and black nationalism that does not claim racial superiority, which differ in detail. Most answers outside race, separatism, religion and family are inferred and low confidence.

sources.usedFor: The Nation's own statement on separation, a separate state, self-defense, voting, intermarriage and economics.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement's economic emphasis was on black-owned businesses and jobs it created itself, not on wage law; no stated position, so adherents plausibly split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Elijah Muhammad promoted black capitalism through bakeries, groceries and farms, yet also demanded state-funded reparations; no doctrine on markets versus government in general.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Nation bought land, farms and businesses and urged black people to own and control economic resources, implying respect for property, though it also demanded land from the state.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Nation preached self-reliance and criticized dependence on white society, but also demanded state support and reparations for black Americans, so the answer is split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective black-owned enterprise was encouraged, but no worker-ownership doctrine appears in the sources.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Elijah Muhammad enforced strict bans on alcohol, drugs and pork among members, treating intoxicants as a tool of black degradation.

state-harmful.rationale: The Nation demanded its own state and a separate territory, so it rejects statelessness even while condemning the existing white-run state.

limit-guns.rationale: Malcolm X for the Nation insisted black people have the right to defend themselves, and the Fruit of Islam served as a self-defense arm.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Police are portrayed as successors to slave-era enforcers who traded bloodhounds for police dogs, and Muhammad told followers not to serve in the armed forces.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Nation required sexual abstinence before marriage and monogamy within it, so legal sex work conflicts with its moral code.

traditional-family.rationale: Muhammad's teaching prescribed patriarchal roles, male providers, female homemakers, monogamy and chastity before marriage.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Nation sought an Islam-based black nation and condemned Christianity as the white man's tool, so religion-informed public life is favored for its own faith, but a larger role for existing religion is not the aim.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Core demand: a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation, as redress for slavery.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Nation rejected white American culture and sought its own black national culture, so the statement splits depending on which nation is meant. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

gradual-change.rationale: Malcolm X dismissed integration gains as tokenism and said white rule was scheduled to end, and Muhammad foresaw its imminent destruction.

open-borders.rationale: The Nation's program is separation of the races into distinct territories, the opposite of open borders.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mixed: Yakub's story centres on a scientist, yet the Nation's expectation is divine intervention by the Mother Plane.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power never figures in the Nation's teaching; no basis for a position, so neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that white rule would be ended by divine action and urged restraint, while Malcolm X asserted self-defense; adherents are split on human revolution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Nation ran businesses, paid work and tithes; abolition of money is foreign to its program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the doctrine; no basis for either side.

democracy-best.rationale: Muslims could register to vote and back chosen candidates, but integrationist democracy was viewed as tokenism and the Nation sought separation.

right-to-secede.rationale: The central political demand was a separate territory for black Americans, a form of secession or partition.

natural-rulers.rationale: The doctrine calls black people the original divine race and says whites were allowed 6,000 years of rule; it ranks races by nature, but it does not say who is suited to govern.

political-violence-never.rationale: Malcolm X on behalf of the Nation asserted a right of self-defense, and the Fruit of Islam was a defense arm; Muhammad nonetheless held back from revolt.

war-builds-character.rationale: Muhammad told followers to refuse draft and military service in American wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: The goal was a separate nation under Islam, as Malcolm X described it, so state and religion are joined.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Nation sought a nation ordered by its own Islamic teachings, though its scripture was distinctive.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The separate-state demand and rejection of integration aim at a nation made up of black people, with whites kept separate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is explained as racial: whites were created to rule for 6,000 years, not by class struggle.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Africanism was rejected by Muhammad, though the Original Asiatic Nation concept spans non-European peoples; split.

direct-action.rationale: Muhammad urged separation and self-help instead of civil-rights marches and criticized King, but also confronted police at times; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no teaching that methods must mirror the desired society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement built farms, schools and businesses; foraging is foreign to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gender-based role divisions were central doctrine, and enterprises were built.

production-for-use.rationale: The Nation ran profit-seeking bakeries and shops without a doctrine of production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Muhammad's analysis of exploitation was racial rather than class-based, and the Nation ran profit-making enterprises.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Nation demanded state funding for a black state, so a general rejection of taxation does not fit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Nation treats the black nation as a collective whose redress and separation are demanded as a group.

conscription.rationale: Muhammad told followers not to register for the draft and served prison time himself for draft evasion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Separation, the right to leave integration behind, is the Nation's answer to its grievances, though the vote is not rejected outright.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Nation of Islam's Yakub teaching holds that whites were bred into a race with a violent and deceitful nature, a claim of inborn racial character; it is a theological origin story rather than a claim about genetic ability, so the fit is close but not exact.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Nation preaches awakening the 'dead' black nation from enslaved decadence to its original divine status.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Nation asked for a defined territory, not expansion abroad; Muhammad spoke of civilizing Africa.

bound-labor.rationale: The Nation's founding grievance is slavery and bondage, so any bound labor is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Nation taught that Christianity and white learning were instruments of white supremacy, and ran its own schools in response.

universal-morality.rationale: The Nation's morality is tied to race and revelation through its messenger, not universal reason.

single-common-good.rationale: No statement on a single reasoned common good; the Nation's concern was the racial interest of black people.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic votes in company management are absent from the Nation's economic teaching.

national-self-determination.rationale: The core demand is a separate state for black Americans governing themselves.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Nation rests on revelation from Fard Muhammad and Elijah Muhammad as messenger, and faith claims such as the Mother Plane.

dominated-front.rationale: Malcolm X and Muhammad framed black Americans and non-European peoples as one 'Original Asiatic' family against white rule, though Pan-Africanism was rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Men are providers, women household keepers, a core feature of Nation teaching.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Nation demanded racial separation, though it asked this as a negotiated separate state rather than white-run Jim Crow, which it also condemned.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Nation sees the state as a white instrument of racial domination, not of class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Nation rejected assimilation into white American culture.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Nation endorsed male headship and does not treat it as an injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Black and white elites are called out, including 'Uncle Tom' leaders and the federal government that will not protect black people.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Nation demanded a state-funded territory and spoke of an expansive moral order, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Members were to marry within the black community, and marrying whites was taboo; Malcolm X said only a man ashamed of himself marries out of his race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Nation teaches blacks divine and whites devils by nature, so equal moral worth is denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Nation had no socialist doctrine, so the question of socialism in one country does not arise.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Nation was a proselytizing faith that sought converts from Christianity.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Nation ran its own religious schools; the statement concerns state schools, on which it did not clearly stake out a view.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is absent from Nation teaching.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Nation was itself persecuted as subversive and was prosecuted for sedition.

separated-powers.rationale: The sources show no teaching on constitutional checks; the Nation sought a state but left its design unspecified.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is blamed on slavery and white domination.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program rests on the claim that integration cannot work and the races must live apart.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is nowhere in the sources; no inference possible.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials does not appear in the sources on the movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Nation supported self-defense and had the Fruit of Islam, yet no stated demand for an armed citizenry.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided-nation reunification has no analogue in Nation teaching.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Nation ranks races, with blacks divine and whites devils, and rejects equality of peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources record no Nation position on capital punishment.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Nation has its own creation account with the Yakub story, but no stated position on public schools.

minority-language-support.rationale: Muhammad's teaching said slavery took black people's language, but no policy on minority language support is recorded.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Nation enforced strict, uniform conduct among members.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Nation said independence needs black economic self-sufficiency, as Malcolm X urged black economic leadership in their own community.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is absent from the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation never appears in the sources.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Nation's teaching holds that whites are devils to be destroyed by divine action and defends self-defense; absolute non-initiation is not its creed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Malcolm X stated that integration will not work and the Nation demanded a separate state rather than a fight for equal rights within white America.

no-bailouts.rationale: No stated position on bailouts; the Nation stressed black self-reliance but said nothing on state rescues.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Malcolm X's 1963 statement limits force to self-defense, and the Nation refused military service; it did not seek to start a revolution by arms.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's schools and teaching centred black history and the Yakub account of race.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Nation taught that white rule was over and whites were devils, so rule over blacks by whites for their benefit is rejected.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Black economic self-reliance and separation from white institutions are core planks of the programme.

recallable-delegates.rationale: No stated position; the Nation was hierarchical internally but rejected white-run representative politics, so adherents' view is unclear.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Self-reliance points to private saving, while the demand for redress from the state points the other way; no stated position.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Nation bought and held farmland privately and demanded a separate state, so it favoured ownership of land by blacks rather than tenure only by use.

single-official-language.rationale: No stated position on a common state language; the Nation taught Arabic as a religious language but did not campaign on state language policy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No documented position; the movement sought black-run institutions free of outside control but distrusted the state.

job-guarantee.rationale: Self-reliance through black-owned business was emphasised over state employment; adherents split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Strict family and gender discipline were central to Elijah Muhammad's teaching.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Nation was a hierarchical organisation led by Elijah Muhammad with the Fruit of Islam, not informal.

religious-nation.rationale: The Nation of Islam defined its community through its religion alongside race, and religion is central to its program.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's program stressed black-owned private business and self-reliance rather than common ownership.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Nation of Islam is a religious movement teaching Islamic doctrine and the Yakub story, so religion is not an illusion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Nation enforced strict gender roles and moral discipline, and held that equality does not need economic transformation.

majority-settlement.rationale: The doctrine rejects integration and favours separation, opposing steering majority settlement into minority regions.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Nation of Islam presented itself as Islam, so it rejects the claim that Islam is incompatible with the West, while also rejecting Western white society.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Nation's program asked for a funded separate state and self-reliance, not a stance on IMF-style loan conditions, and adherents might see them as white power or as a reason for independence.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching imposed strict gender discipline and patriarchal family roles, so it would not frame women's subordination as something to end, though it did not address nature.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Malcolm X's account describes a white-controlled society where blacks lack real voice and power, so a hollow-rights claim would fit, though the press is not specifically discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: No documented position on standing law and judges; the Nation distrusted white-run courts yet demanded equal justice under law, so adherents would not clearly agree or disagree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Nation held that black people were the original, superior race and demanded a separate black state, so political rights confined to one racial group follows from its doctrine, though the program asked for separation rather than a racial franchise within one state.

open-government-data.rationale: Nothing in the Nation's documented program addresses open government records; it distrusted white-run government but did not campaign on transparency.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Nation urged black people to buy from black-owned shops, but its enemy was whites as a race, not a religious minority, and nothing documents shunning of religious-minority shops.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Nation's teaching is religious, built on the worship of Allah and a theology of races, so promoting atheism in schools is opposed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Nation's ministers were men and its teaching assigned women domestic and subordinate roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Nation taught strict gender discipline and the man as head of the family.

rent-control.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses rent controls; adherents are split between wanting state relief and relying on black self-help.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Fruit of Islam trained disciplined, uniformed male members and the Muslim Girls Training classes did the same for girls, which suits the doctrine's strict moral discipline.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that Muslims may defend themselves and should refuse military service; Malcolm X endorsed defence 'by any means necessary', so self-defence is not wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The doctrine claims an unbroken black origin as the original people, though it is a religious lineage story and not a national continuity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught a cosmic struggle between the black original people and the white race of devils, with the end of whites' 6,000-year rule.

god-not-male.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught that Allah appeared in person as a black man, Wallace Fard Muhammad, and God is described as male.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Black economic self-reliance and black-run businesses were core; in a separate black state the economy would be in black hands.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Nation of Islam was a religious movement that taught that politics and the black nation's destiny serve divine ends, so it holds human beings to be spiritual as well as material.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Malcolm X's statement of the Nation's program and Elijah Muhammad's teaching held that black people have distinct interests requiring separation and organisation of their own.

racial-pride.rationale: The Nation of Islam taught that black people are the original and superior race and urged racial pride and self-respect against white supremacy.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Nation refused military service in white America's wars, but its stated position on armed force in general is not a defensive-only rule; adherents are split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Elijah Muhammad urged abstaining from white-run politics and seeking a separate state, so separate electorates are not on point.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The movement saw the white-run state as hostile but its concern was white rule, not partition of the country.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Nation of Islam urged black self-defense and would not accept a white state's monopoly on force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Elijah Muhammad refused the draft and Nation members refused service in white America's wars.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The Nation addressed no fiscal rules; no inference is possible.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Yakub doctrine holds that blacks are the original divine race and whites a bred race of devils, denying a shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The Nation did not address public broadcasting; adherents distrust white-run media but the question is untouched.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Under Elijah Muhammad the Nation taught Islam as the true religion of the black man and condemned Christianity as the slave-master's religion, so it rejects equal-truth pluralism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Elijah Muhammad stressed black farming and land ownership, but the sources show no position on state price supports; adherents distrusted white-run government.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Nation refused military service and stressed self-defense; no stated view on nuclear arms, so split.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Nation taught strict gender roles and male protection of women, but black land ownership was a goal; no stated view on inheritance.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Nation distrusted electoral politics and abstained from it, but did not theorise democracy as procedure; split or indifferent.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Nation enforced strict sexual and gender discipline and confined sex to marriage.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's vote was not an issue for the Nation, which stressed separate gender roles but abstained from politics generally.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Yakub myth teaches that races are real, bred groupings with inherent differences, the opposite of a constructed-category view.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: No stated position; the movement distrusted white-run institutions, yet condemned white crimes against black people.

indirect-election.rationale: No stated position; the Nation had its own appointed hierarchy but made no case on electoral mechanics.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: No stated position on colonial borders; adherents would be split between Pan-African and separatist views.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Nation's separatist, anti-white-world outlook had no stated China policy; adherents are split or indifferent, so neutral.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Nation is itself a religiously defined movement whose racial theology is its politics, so it does not separate politics from religion.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Nation of Islam held that whites had unjustly enriched themselves from slavery and demanded land and funding in redress, so process alone does not justify a distribution.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that the white race was devils and that oppression by whites continued, so racism is the main obstacle.

police-more-powers.rationale: Police are portrayed as successors to slave-era enforcers who traded bloodhounds for police dogs, and Muhammad told followers not to serve in the armed forces. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Nation preached self-reliance and criticized dependence on white society, but also demanded state support and reparations for black Americans, so the answer is split. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Some races are inherently superior to others.
missingStatements.rationale: The central doctrine is that black people are the original, divine race and whites an engineered race of devils.

missingStatements.text: Black Americans should receive land and public funding for a separate state of their own.
missingStatements.rationale: The Muslim Program demanded a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific historical demand of the Nation of Islam program, too narrow for the bank; reparations and separatism are covered by colonial-reparations and ethnic-nation.

missingStatements.text: Racial integration is neither possible nor desirable.
missingStatements.rationale: Malcolm X said integration will not work and called gains tokenism.

notes: Black supremacy is a label applied by outside watchdogs and used by a few historical figures such as Leonard Howell; it is not one organised ideology. After 1975 the Nation of Islam under W. Deen Mohammed dropped the doctrine and Louis Farrakhan's revived Nation retained it. Answers on most economic and institutional questions are inferences.
